stories.headline: Forty-two lines to a page: the book that started the press
stories.summary: The Gutenberg Bible, printed in the 1450s by Johannes Gutenberg in Mainz, was the earliest major book printed in Europe using mass-produced metal movable type. Most of its pages carry 42 lines, giving it the name 42-line Bible, and a complete copy has 1,288 pages, usually bound in two volumes. Of the 158 or 180 copies originally printed, 49 survive in at least substantial portion.

stories.headline: The tallest thing on Earth for 3,700 years
stories.summary: The Great Pyramid of Giza was built around 2600 BC, over about 26 years, as the tomb of the pharaoh Khufu. Initially standing at 146.6 metres, it was the world's tallest human-made structure for more than 3,700 years. Over time most of its smooth white limestone casing was removed, lowering it to the current 138.5 metres.

stories.headline: A citadel on a ridge above the Urubamba
stories.summary: Machu Picchu is a 15th-century Inca citadel on a mountain ridge at 2,430 metres in southern Peru, about 80 km north-west of Cusco, above the Urubamba River. Estimated to have been built around 1450, it is believed to have served as an estate for the Inca emperor Pachacuti, and it was abandoned roughly a century later.
